mit-fact-01.text: A decision after a hearing, panel meeting, or sanctioning panel to suspend (including a suspension held in abeyance), expel, revoke a degree, suspend or revoke recognition of a student group, or terminate approval of a student organization residence may be appealed by the respondent to the Chancellor; in all other cases, the COD decision is final unless otherwise specifically noted.
mit-fact-01.summaryZh: COD 指定的严重处分决定可向 Chancellor 申诉；并非每项 COD 决定都有申诉权，特殊案件另有规定。
mit-fact-01.scope: Committee on Discipline; students and student organizations; respondent appeal of specific severe sanctions Only enumerated severe sanctions; special Section XIII rules include complainant/Title IX and other sexual-misconduct-related routes; not universal denial of appeal.

evidence.quote:
A decision after a hearing, panel meeting, or sanctioning panel to suspend (including a suspension held in abeyance) or expel a student, revoke a degree, suspend (including a suspension held in abeyance) or revoke recognition of a student group, or terminate approval of a student organization residence may be appealed by the respondent to the Chancellor. In all other cases, the COD decision is final, unless otherwise specifically noted (see Section XIII for special rules regarding appeals in cases involving sexual misconduct, sexual harassment, intimate partner violence, stalking, and Title IX Sexual Harassment).
All appeals must be submitted in writing to the OSCCS staff by the appealing party (usually the respondent; see Section XIII for situations when the complainant may appeal) within five business days of the date the appealing party received the letter advising them of the decision of the COD.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 35–36

deadline.en: For eligible COD appeals: submit in writing to OSCCS within five business days of receiving the decision letter. Only the listed decisions are appealable; Section XIII has special rules.
deadline.zh: 适用的 COD 申诉：收到决定信后五个工作日内，书面提交 OSCCS。仅限列举的可申诉决定；Section XIII 特殊规定须另查。
deadline.quote: All appeals must be submitted in writing to the OSCCS staff by the appealing party (usually the respondent; see Section XIII for situations when the complainant may appeal) within five business days of the date the appealing party received the letter advising them of the decision of the COD.

mit-fact-02.text: For COD appeals that are available under the captured Rules, four ordinary grounds are specified: substantive relevant information unavailable at decision; substantial procedural departure significantly affecting fairness; a material finding substantially against the evidence; or a sanction at significant variance with the appropriate range. Appeal availability is limited to the listed serious decisions, with other decisions final unless specifically noted; special sexual-misconduct/TitleIX rules include additional or modified grounds.
mit-fact-02.summaryZh: 适用的 COD 申诉须基于规定理由；案件类别与决定类型决定能否申诉。
mit-fact-02.scope: MIT Committee on Discipline; students and student organizations; Captured COD appeal grounds; scope and appeal availability limited by RulesXII and special provisions, not a right to appeal every COD decision.

evidence.quote:
A. Appeals may only be made on one or more of the following grounds:
there exists substantive and relevant information that was not available at the time of the decision
a. In cases involving complaints of Title IX Sexual Harassment, this includes new evidence that was not reasonably available at the time the determination regarding responsibility or dismissal was made that could affect the outcome of the matter.
there was a substantial departure from the COD rules and procedures that significantly affected the fairness of the process;
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 38–41

evidence.quote:
a material finding that formed a basis for the COD’s decision was substantially against the weight of the evidence that was before the COD when it made the decision; and/or
the sanction is at significant variance with the range of sanctions appropriate in the situation.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 43–44

evidence.quote:
XII. Appeals
A decision after a hearing, panel meeting, or sanctioning panel to suspend (including a suspension held in abeyance) or expel a student, revoke a degree, suspend (including a suspension held in abeyance) or revoke recognition of a student group, or terminate approval of a student organization residence may be appealed by the respondent to the Chancellor. In all other cases, the COD decision is final, unless otherwise specifically noted (see Section XIII for special rules regarding appeals in cases involving sexual misconduct, sexual harassment, intimate partner violence, stalking, and Title IX Sexual Harassment).
All appeals must be submitted in writing to the OSCCS staff by the appealing party (usually the respondent; see Section XIII for situations when the complainant may appeal) within five business days of the date the appealing party received the letter advising them of the decision of the COD.
In the event IDHR dismisses a complaint of Title IX Sexual Harassment following an initial assessment, the dismissal may be appealed by either party in accordance with the processes established by IDHR.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 34–37

evidence.quote:
In cases involving complaints of Title IX Sexual Harassment, a party may also appeal on the additional ground that the Title IX Coordinator, the investigator(s), or the decision-maker(s) had a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or the individual complainant or respondent that affected the outcome of the matter.
B .The Chancellor makes a decision based upon the written appeal(s) providing the ground(s) on which the party is relying for appeal, and as much of the record of the COD hearing or sanctioning panel of the case as the Chancellor determines it is appropriate to consider.
C. The Chancellor will consult with the Chair on all appeals. The Chancellor may also confer with other participants in the hearing or sanctioning panel and, in sexual misconduct cases, with the Title IX Coordinator and/or the investigator(s).
D. Before modifying or overruling a decision of the COD, the Chancellor will meet with available members of the COD who decided the case and will make a final decision after consulting with them.
E. The final decision will be communicated in writing to the same people who received written notice of the COD decision (including simultaneously to both the complainant and the respondent in all cases involving complaints of sexual misconduct, sexual harassment, intimate partner violence, stalking, and Title IX Sexual Harassment), and to any other officials of MIT who need to be aware of it in order to permit them to fulfill their professional responsibilities. When it is reasonable, a member of the OSCCS staff shall meet with the parties regarding any appeal decision.
F. This appellate decision by the Chancellor is final.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 45–50

evidence.quote: H. No appeal is available for the decision of (i) the COD to resolve a complaint, either in whole or in part, by making recommendations to MIT Senior Leadership, or (ii) MIT Senior Leadership to accept, reject, or modify a recommendation of the COD under Section XI.L.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 52–52

mit-fact-05.text: Failure to complete or comply with COD sanctions may result in an enrollment hold, revision of the sanction, or further disciplinary action, as determined by the Chair.
mit-fact-05.summaryZh: 未完成或遵守 COD 处分要求，可能导致注册限制、处分调整或进一步纪律措施。
mit-fact-05.scope: Committee on Discipline; respondents with assigned sanctions;

evidence.quote: Respondents are required to complete and/or comply with COD sanctions. Failure to complete or comply with sanctions may result in an enrollment hold, revision of the sanction, or further disciplinary action, as determined by the Chair. The Chair may consult with other COD members as needed if revising any sanction or taking further disciplinary action.
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 35–35

mit-fact-11.text: MIT students who are victims of misconduct or responding to an allegation of policy violation are encouraged by the COD to seek personal support through resources including Mental Health and Counseling, Alcohol and Other Drug Services, Violence Prevention and Response, and Chaplains.
mit-fact-11.summaryZh: 收到指控或受到不当行为影响的学生，可寻求 COD 列出的个人支持服务。
mit-fact-11.scope: Committee on Discipline; victims and respondents in disciplinary processes;

evidence.quote:
Personal Support
The COD recognizes that it can often be difficult to find yourself the victim of misconduct or responding to an allegation that you violated MIT policy. The COD encourages you to seek and receive personal support during this process. Resources at MIT for this include:
Mental Health and Counseling
Alcohol and Other Drug Services
Violence Prevention and Response
Chaplains
evidence.location: Published supplemental locator: lines 29–34

clm-imperial-college-london-academic-mis.text: Imperial's Academic Misconduct procedures govern the investigation of suspected misconduct, potential sanctions, and applicable appeal rights. Students challenging an Academic Misconduct Panel decision must submit an appeal within ten College working days of notification; the general academic-results appeal procedure (with a 15 working-day window) does not apply to misconduct decisions. Potential misconduct in postgraduate research programmes is dealt with under Ordinance D17; the ten-day statement does not establish a deadline for that separate procedure.

evidence.quote: To make an appeal you must submit the appeal form below to student.appeals@imperial.ac.uk within the deadline you have been given and including all documentation regarding the allegation and decision. You should also include any additional documentation that is relevant to the details of your appeal statement.
evidence.location: Academic misconduct procedures and appeals; captured normalized text line 00227

evidence.quote: If the student wishes to appeal against the decision of the Academic Misconduct Panel, they must submit the appeal form (Appendix III) to student.appeals@imperial.ac.uk within ten College working days of receiving the decision of the Academic Misconduct Panel.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy and Procedure v1.3; PDF actual page 9, Sections 48 & 51

evidence.quote: Potential academic misconduct in postgraduate research programmes will be dealt with under ordinance D17, The Investigation of Allegations of Research Misconduct.
evidence.location: Academic Misconduct Policy and Procedure v1.3; PDF actual page 2, Section 13

clm-imperial-college-london-academic-mis.summaryZh: 学术不端委员会决定的申诉期限为收到决定后十个 College 工作日；普通成绩申诉与研究生科研不端适用不同程序。

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-acknowled.text: Imperial Library guidance advises students to acknowledge generative AI use in assessed work and outlines recommended elements. When dAIsy is permitted for assessed work, its Use Policy requires students to acknowledge AI use and maintain transparency. Specific requirements and formats are determined by departments, courses, or assessment briefs.

evidence.quote: A statement of acknowledgment shows the reader which AI tool you used and for what specific purpose. You should include a statement to acknowledge your use of generative AI tools for all assessed work, in accordance with guidelines from your department or course team.
evidence.location: Acknowledging and referencing use; captured normalized text line 00289

evidence.quote: Expectations regarding the disclosure or acknowledgement of GenAI use vary across disciplines, assessments, publishers, funders, and professional contexts. Students and staff should therefore familiarise themselves with any applicable requirements and ensure that their use of GenAI is appropriately documented where required.
evidence.location: Expectations regarding disclosure; captured normalized text line 00122

evidence.quote: ii) Academic integrity and referencing - Where GenAI use is permitted for assessed work, acknowledge it (e.g., tool, version, prompt approach). Improper use can be investigated under University Academic Misconduct procedures [PDF].
evidence.location: Responsible uses; captured normalized text line 00603 (Section 5(ii))

evidence.quote: When communicating externally, do not present dAIsy outputs as Imperial’s position without approval. For assessed work where AI use is permitted, be transparent about how you used AI.
evidence.location: Communications and transparency; captured normalized text line 00627 (Section 13)

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-acknowled.summaryZh: 图书馆建议注明 AI 辅助；获准在考核中使用 dAIsy 时，其条款要求披露。格式取决于院系、课程和考核说明。

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-detection.text: For the 2026–27 academic year, Imperial states that it does not use Turnitin's AI-writing detection functionality as part of its assessment processes. Academic-integrity concerns are evaluated by staff using academic judgement and evidence. This statement does not exclude authenticity interviews or other permitted investigative methods.

evidence.quote: We would like to reassure students that Imperial does not use Turnitin's AI writing detection tool as part of its assessment processes. Decisions relating to academic integrity are made by staff using academic judgement and evidence, and following our institution policies.
evidence.location: Turnitin EULA changes; captured normalized text line 00147

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-detection.summaryZh: 2026–27 学年 Imperial 不在考核流程中使用 Turnitin AI 写作检测。教师仍可按证据及适用程序调查疑虑。

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-misconduc.text: Unless explicitly authorised, using artificial intelligence to create assessed work may be treated as an offence such as contract cheating under Imperial's Plagiarism, Academic Integrity & Exam Offences regulations.

evidence.quote: Unless explicitly authorised, using AI to create assessed work may be treated as an offence such as contract cheating under Imperial’s Plagiarism, Academic Integrity & Exam Offences regulations.
evidence.location: Appropriate academic use; captured normalized text line 00285

clm-imperial-college-london-ai-misconduc.summaryZh: 未经明确授权，用 AI 生成考核作品可能构成学术不端，并非使用 AI 就自动受罚。

clm-imperial-college-london-daisy-copyri.text: Users of Imperial's dAIsy platform must not upload third-party content they are not permitted to share. Reuse of AI outputs must comply with licensing and academic citation norms. When communicating externally, dAIsy outputs must not be presented as Imperial's position without approval.

evidence.quote: Do not upload third-party content you are not permitted to share. Ensure that any reuse of AI outputs complies with licensing and academic citation norms.
evidence.location: Copyright and IP; captured normalized text line 00625 (Section 12)

evidence.quote: When communicating externally, do not present dAIsy outputs as Imperial’s position without approval. For assessed work where AI use is permitted, be transparent about how you used AI.
evidence.location: Communications and transparency; captured normalized text line 00627 (Section 13)

clm-imperial-college-london-daisy-copyri.summaryZh: 不得上传无权分享的第三方内容；输出再用须符合许可和引用规范。

clm-imperial-college-london-daisy-sancti.text: Breaches of Imperial's dAIsy Use Policy may lead to action under Academic Misconduct procedures for students and HR/disciplinary processes for staff, as well as under Information Security and Data Protection policies. Sanctions may include removal of access, grade penalties, or formal disciplinary measures.

evidence.quote: Breaches may lead to action under Academic Misconduct (students) and HR/disciplinary processes (staff), as well as Information Security and Data Protection policies. Sanctions may include removal of access, grade penalties, or formal disciplinary measures.
evidence.location: Compliance and sanctions; captured normalized text line 00629 (Section 14)

clm-imperial-college-london-daisy-sancti.summaryZh: 违反 dAIsy 条款可能导致访问移除、成绩影响或纪律处理，适用程序取决于学生、员工及违规情境。

clm-imperial-college-london-dept-assessm.text: Individual Imperial departments may allow or prohibit generative AI for specific assessments; students must follow the assessment brief and local instructions. The dAIsy Use Policy complements existing university policies and does not replace them; university policy prevails where there is a conflict.

evidence.quote: i) Assessment-related use- Individual departments may allow or prohibit GenAI for specific assessments; local (team/department/faculty) instructions take precedence. Always check the brief and acknowledge permitted AI use as directed.
evidence.location: Responsible uses; captured normalized text line 00602 (Section 5(i))

evidence.quote: It complements, and does not replace, existing Imperial policies on academic integrity, assessment, research ethics, information security, GenAI, and data protection. Where there is any conflict, University policy prevails.
evidence.location: dAIsy Use Policy Section 1; captured normalized text line 00582

clm-imperial-college-london-dept-assessm.summaryZh: 院系可对不同考核允许或禁止 AI；须遵守适用的考核说明，大学政策优先于 dAIsy 使用条款。

clm-imperial-college-london-user-account.text: Users of Imperial's dAIsy AI platform must always apply critical judgment to AI outputs. Generative AI can produce inaccurate or biased outputs ('hallucinate'), omit context, or reflect training-data biases. Users remain accountable for the accuracy, legality, and appropriateness of any content they submit or share through the platform.

evidence.quote: Always apply critical judgement. GenAI can ‘hallucinate’, omit context, or reflect training-data biases. Users remain accountable for the accuracy, legality, and appropriateness of any content they submit or share.
evidence.location: Quality, bias and human oversight; captured normalized text line 00617 (Section 9)

clm-imperial-college-london-user-account.summaryZh: dAIsy 用户须批判性核实输出，并对准确性、合法性及适当性负责。

coursework.zh: 能否使用 AI 由院系和这项考核的说明决定；未获授权的生成内容可能涉及学术不端。

exams.zh: 当前已审核记录未建立统一的考试许可或禁令。请查本次考试说明，工具可访问不等于考试可用。
exams.en: The reviewed record establishes no universal exam permission or ban. Check the particular exam instructions.

exams.meaningEn: Not mentioned is an evidence gap, not permission or proof that no exam rules exist.

disclosure.zh: 图书馆建议注明 AI 辅助；获准在考核中使用 dAIsy 时必须注明，具体内容按考核说明。

privacy_data.en: dAIsy is approved for unrestricted data. Copilot protection, logging and web-search conditions need separate checks.

privacy_data.meaningEn: Restrictions depend on data class and tool features; an institutional login does not approve sensitive data.

approved_tools.zh: 师生有 dAIsy 基础访问，Developer 权限限获批员工，并受 token 额度约束；访问不授予考核许可。
approved_tools.en: dAIsy Basic access is for staff and students; Developer access is for approved staff, with token limits.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 这里描述服务访问条件，作业与考试许可另查。

research_publication.zh: 涉及个人资料、敏感主题或参与者的科研，使用 AI 前可能需要伦理审批、DPIA 和数据治理措施。
research_publication.en: Research involving people or sensitive data may need ethics approval, a DPIA and data-governance controls.
research_publication.meaningZh: 是否需要审批取决于研究情境，并非每次 AI 使用都须完成同一套程序。
research_publication.meaningEn: Approval requirements depend on the research; not every AI use needs the same process.

academic_integrity.zh: 区分检测证据、学术不端调查及申诉。十个 College 工作日期限不适用于所有成绩或科研争议。
academic_integrity.en: Distinguish detection evidence, misconduct investigations and appeals; the ten-day rule has a specific procedure.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 一般纪律规则不是 AI 专属自动处罚；研究生科研案件走 D17。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: General disciplinary rules are not automatic AI penalties; postgraduate research cases follow D17.

teaching_guidance.zh: 学校提供生成式 AI 教学原则；具体考核许可仍按院系、课程和任务规定。
teaching_guidance.en: University GenAI principles guide teaching; permission still depends on the course and task.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 原则框架本身不提供作业或考试的通用使用许可。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: A principles framework does not establish general assessment permission.

security_procurement.zh: dAIsy 在 Imperial 基础设施中使用 SSO 和审计日志；资料处理须遵守机构 IT 使用条件。
security_procurement.en: dAIsy uses SSO and audit logs within Imperial infrastructure, under institutional IT conditions.
security_procurement.meaningZh: 不用于训练与无日志并非同一件事；获准使用工具不代表任何资料都可输入。
security_procurement.meaningEn: No model training does not mean no logging, and tool access is not approval for every data class.

do.en: Check your course syllabus for permitted AI scope and reporting rules (§2(5)).
do.zh: 查阅课程大纲，确认允许的 AI 范围并按规定方式报告（§2(5)）。

do.en: Verify facts/sources, keep process drafts, and check funder/journal rules in research (§1(2), §3(7)).
do.zh: 核实事实与出处、保留草稿记录，并在科研中预先核对资助方与期刊规定（§1(2)、§3(7)）。

do.en: Comply with privacy/copyright rules and prevent leakage of sensitive research data (§1(3), §3(4)).
do.zh: 遵守隐私与著作权规定，防止敏感科研信息外泄并避免不必要地输入研究数据（§1(3)、§3(4)）。

dont.en: Do not treat campus ChatGPT Edu or Codex access as coursework or exam permission.
dont.zh: 不要把学校提供的 ChatGPT Edu 或 Codex 权限当作课程作业或考试许可。

dont.en: Do not use AI in violation of instructor restrictions; it may be deemed an ethics violation and may result in disadvantages (§2(7)).
dont.zh: 不要违反教师限制使用 AI；此类行为可能被认定为违反学习伦理并可能受到不利处理（§2(7)）。

dont.en: Do not upload subscribed library e-resources to AI tools or run automated DOI scrapers.
dont.zh: 不要将图书馆订阅电子资源上传至 AI 服务或使用自动化工具批量抓取。

scope.en: SNU's AI Guidelines (enacted Jan. 1, 2026) set voluntary principles: instructors should state course AI rules in syllabi (§2(1)–(2)) and students must comply and report when required (§2(5)). Campus ChatGPT Edu or Codex access is not assessment permission; research language-editing (§3(3) Footnote 1), research data protection (§3(4)), and Library e-resource licenses have specific conditions.
scope.zh: 首尔大学《AI 指南》（2026 年 1 月 1 日制定）确立自主原则：教师应在课程大纲中说明 AI 规则（§2(1)–(2)），学生必须遵守并在要求时报告（§2(5)）。校内 ChatGPT Edu 或 Codex 权限不代表考核许可；科研外语润色（§3(3) 脚注 1）、科研数据保护（§3(4)）及图书馆电子资源许可各有具体条件。

cl-seoul-national-university-chatgpt-224.text: Seoul National University provides ChatGPT Edu (including Codex software development support) for a 15-month operational period (June 2026 – August 2027) to currently enrolled students and employed faculty and researchers via administrator batch registration (administrative staff apply individually; affiliated school teachers receive ChatGPT Plus by application; members on academic or employment leave (휴학·휴직) are excluded). The SNU press release states the service is provided free of charge to students and excludes user input/output data from model training; accounts inactive for 3 or more months are subject to ID recall.
cl-seoul-national-university-chatgpt-224.scope: Enrolled students, employed faculty/researchers, and applying staff (members on leave/suspension excluded); institutional access does not grant coursework or exam permission

claim-snu-002a.text: SNU's AI Guidelines present voluntary principles rather than uniform prohibitions or restrictions on AI use, supporting context-specific judgment, creative approaches, and clear communication grounded in academic autonomy, trust, and social responsibility.
claim-snu-002a.scope: All intramural members (faculty, students, researchers, developers, administrative staff) and SNU-led collaborations

evidence.quote:
The purpose of these Guidelines is to set forth principles for the appropriate use of AI across
education and learning, research and development, and administrative functions, and to issue
recommendations for putting those principles into practice. Rather than imposing uniform
prohibitions or restrictions on AI use, the Guidelines are intended to support context-specific
judgment, creative approaches, and clear communication. The use of AI should respect the
autonomy of University members, grounded in the trust that underpins the University’s academic
community, and should be carried out in a manner that harmonizes creative scholarly activity with
social responsibility.
evidence.location: Physical page 1; Preamble, Paragraph 4 (Purpose & Non-Uniform Restriction); Extracted text SHA256 8339b710951123c45cb0ad432f2de0f2b56ef00ae01eb99cca03b511e2c44cd5; original binding lines 28–35; characters 2228–2906; excerpt offset 0–678

claim-snu-002d.scope: All intramural members across education, research, and administration

evidence.quote:

do.en: Always verify the designated AI assessment category (A, B, C, or D) in the course unit handbook and Canvas assessment brief before starting coursework (DocID 79331 §2.1.1, §2.1.3).
do.zh: 在开始任何课程作业前，务必查阅 Canvas 考核说明及课程大纲，核准依据 DocID 79331 §2.1.1 与 §2.1.3 明确标注的具体 AI 分类（A、B、C 或 D）。

do.en: Acknowledge AI use following University Library guidance: cite direct text/image use formally, provide an overview acknowledgement when asked or appropriate, and include prompts/outputs in an appendix when referencing AI as personal communication or required by School instructions.
do.zh: 遵循大学图书馆指南对 AI 使用进行规范引用与致谢：直接使用 AI 文本或图像须按规范正式引用；在被要求或适当时于文首或脚注提供致谢概述；当作为个人通信引用或学院有要求时，附上包含提示词与输出的附录。

do.en: Use your University IT account to access Microsoft Copilot Chat for commercial data protection; if uploading taught session recordings for study assistance, use University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot (DocID 79331 §2.2.2).
do.zh: 使用大学统一身份账户登录 Microsoft Copilot Chat 以享受商业数据保护；若需上传课程录像辅助学习，须依据 DocID 79331 §2.2.2 使用学校提供的 Microsoft 365 Copilot。

dont.en: Never upload University copyright materials—including lecture recordings, slides, handouts, and exam questions—to external AI tools (DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c)); teaching staff handling student-identifiable data must exclusively use M365 Copilot (§2.3.1).
dont.zh: 依据 DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c)，严禁向外部 AI 工具上传属于曼大版权的材料（包括课程录像、课件、讲义与试卷）；在教学活动中处理可识别学生身份数据的教职工必须专设使用学校提供的 M365 Copilot（§2.3.1）。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in Category A (Prohibited) assessments (even for proofreading or spelling/grammar correction), or beyond surface presentation in Category B (Minimal); note that student choice not to use AI does not apply to Category D (Integrated).
dont.zh: 严禁在类别 A（严禁使用）考核中使用任何生成式 AI（包括校对润色或语法拼写纠正）；在类别 B（最低限度）中严禁超越表层排版呈现去改动论点观点；同时注意 §2.1.2 赋予的不使用 AI 选择权不适用于类别 D（深度融合）。

dont.en: Do not present unacknowledged AI-generated content as your own (an indicator of academic malpractice under DocID 639 §3.1.3.6); markers rely on academic judgement and Turnitin similarity as the University does not use software claiming to detect GenAI (§4.2.2).
dont.zh: 切勿将未经披露的 AI 生成内容作为个人成果提交（属 DocID 639 §3.1.3.6 明确的学术不端指标）；评卷人依靠学术判断与 Turnitin 相似度比对，大学依据 §4.2.2 明确不使用声称能检测生成式 AI 的软件。

clm-man-authorship-viva-voce.text: Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).
clm-man-authorship-viva-voce.scope: Optional authorship viva voce trigger, 30-working-day post-feedback-deadline timing, 5-working-day notice, support-only accompaniment, reasonable adjustments, non-punitive viva outcome, and AUO case handling

do.en: Check the specific Moodle statement (Without Limits, Guided, or Must Not Be Used) before using AI.
do.zh: 在开始每项作业前，务必核对 Moodle 标注的标准 AI 声明（无限制、引导使用或严禁使用）。

do.en: Follow task instructions, acknowledge the AI tool and its contribution, cite when necessary, and acknowledge non-use if AI was permitted but unused.
do.zh: 遵循任务说明，书面注明所用 AI 及贡献程度，必要时引用；任务允许但未使用 AI 时也应声明未使用。

do.en: Use Monash enterprise logins for commercial data protection and protect confidential research and personal data.
do.zh: 使用莫纳什官方账号激活商业数据保护，严禁向外部 AI 工具上传个人隐私、版权课件或机密科研数据。

dont.en: Do not treat campus Microsoft Copilot or Google Gemini access as coursework assessment permission.
dont.zh: 不要把学校提供的 Copilot 或 Gemini 账号权限当作课程作业的使用许可。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI or unapproved browser plugins in scheduled eExams unless authorized on landing page.
dont.zh: 严禁在电子期末考试（eExam）中使用生成式 AI 或未授权插件，除非考试首页明确允许。

dont.en: Do not use AI to rewrite text or change words under the guise of proofreading (§4.6).
dont.zh: 严禁以润色为名利用 AI 重写段落、换词或生成实质内容（润色仅限于识别拼写和语法错漏，§4.6）。

scope.en: Monash University delegates assessment conditions to Chief Examiners via four standard Moodle statements (§1.7.1–1.7.2). Enterprise Copilot and Gemini access is not assessment permission. Proofreading is strictly limited to identifying spelling and grammar errors (§4.6), AI detection software is barred from misconduct evidence, and unacknowledged use is a breach under §4.7.
scope.zh: 莫纳什大学依据《考核制度程序》§1.7.1–1.7.2 由课程主任通过四类标准 Moodle 声明设定 AI 规则。校方企业级 Copilot 与 Gemini 权限不构成考核许可。润色仅严格限于拼写与语法错漏识别（§4.6），AI 检测工具严禁作为不端证据，未声明使用属于违规行为（§4.7）。

alt.zh: 莫纳什大学依据《考核制度程序》§1.7.1–1.7.2 由课程主任通过四类标准 Moodle 声明设定 AI 规则。校方企业级 Copilot 与 Gemini 权限不构成考核许可。润色仅严格限于拼写与语法错漏识别（§4.6），AI 检测工具严禁作为不端证据，未声明使用属于违规行为（§4.7）。

do.en: Get express permission from your instructor, supervisor, or program before using GenAI in assessed work, and check the course syllabus statement (Senate V-130 / O-130.1).
do.zh: 在评分考核作品中使用生成式 AI 前必须获得授课教师、导师或项目明确许可，并查阅课程大纲中的 GenAI 说明条款（参议院 V-130 / O-130.1）。

do.en: Follow course acknowledgement rules when AI is permitted, and in UBC Vancouver Graduate School theses declare each AI tool and purpose in the Preface (or state non-use).
do.zh: 在获准使用 AI 的课程中遵守标注规范；在 UBC 温哥华校区研究生院学位论文前言中列明每种工具与用途（或明确声明未使用）。

do.en: Check purpose-specific UBC privacy approval; in instructor-required course use of Copilot for Organizations, required student inputs are limited to U1 Low Risk information.
do.zh: 核实符合具体用途的 UBC 隐私审批；教师强制课程使用 Copilot for Organizations 时，可要求学生输入的内容限于 U1 低风险信息。

dont.en: Do not enter personal, confidential, or student grading data into uncleared AI tools, and do not require students to sign up for ChatGPT 5 with an account in a course.
dont.zh: 切勿将个人信息、机密资料或学生成绩输入未经 PIA 审批的 AI 工具，且不得在课程中强制要求学生注册使用 ChatGPT 5 有账号版本。

dont.en: Do not treat institutional access to Copilot Chat (Basic) or CTLT low-risk PIA status for ChatGPT 5 (Without An Account) as permission to use AI on assessed work.
dont.zh: 切勿将机构的 Copilot Chat（Basic）访问权限或 CTLT 对 ChatGPT 5（无账号版）的低风险 PIA 状态视作可在考核作业中使用 AI 的许可。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in examinations or assignments without express permission; unauthorized use is subject to Academic Calendar misconduct and §11 appeal rules.
dont.zh: 未经明确许可切勿在考试或作业中使用生成式 AI；违规使用将按《大学历书》学术不端规章及第 11 节申诉程序处理。

scope.en: Vancouver and Okanagan Senate syllabus policies V-130 and O-130.1 (effective Sept. 1, 2026 for credit-bearing courses, subject to Section 4 consultation exception and graduate thesis exemption), instructor assessment permission rules, Microsoft Copilot Basic vs faculty/staff Premium tiers, UBC Vancouver Graduate School thesis Preface disclosures, and Academic Calendar §11 disciplinary appeal regimes.
scope.zh: 涵盖 UBC 温哥华与奥肯那根参议院课程大纲政策 V-130 与 O-130.1（2026 年 9 月 1 日起对学分课程生效，含第 4 条协商例外及研究生论文豁免）、教师考核许可原则、Microsoft Copilot Basic 与教职工 Premium 分级、温哥华研究生院论文前言披露及《大学历书》第 11 节两套纪律申诉规则。

For Vancouver, any appeal involving allegations before 1 August 2019 uses the historical rules; the revised rules apply only to appeals involving solely allegations on or after 1 August 2019. do.en: Check your school-specific policy and course syllabus before using generative AI in coursework: adhering schools under CSSI Standards & Discipline require prior instructor authorization, while Columbia Law School allows defined research/writing support by default unless the instructor restricts it.
do.zh: 在课程作业中使用生成式 AI 前，请核对所在学院具体规范及课程大纲：采纳 CSSI《学生纪律规范》的学院默认须获教师事先授权，而哥大法学院默认允许既定研究与写作辅助（教师另有要求除外）。

do.en: Disclose any generative AI use contributing to your work product as required by your school (mandatory at Columbia Law School §7; required under CBS Honor Code when permitted), and follow course citation protocols.
do.zh: 按所在学院要求如实披露协助完成学业成果的 AI 使用情况（哥大法学院第 7 条强制要求；商学院获批使用时依据荣誉准则必须规范引用），并遵守具体引注规范。

do.en: Check the exact data class, account, approved model and feature before entering research, client or health information; a product name or BAA alone is insufficient.
do.zh: 输入科研、客户或健康资料前，核对数据分类、具体账号及获批模型和功能；不能仅凭产品名称或 BAA 推定许可。

dont.en: Do not assume AI is permitted in an examination: follow your school and course rules, including written-permission conditions and Law School default-policy exceptions.
dont.zh: 不要假定考试允许使用 AI；须遵循所在学院和课程的规定，包括书面许可条件及法学院默认政策的例外。

dont.en: Do not submit AI-generated text as your own independent work; under Columbia Law School rules, submitting machine-translated drafts of non-English writing as original English work is expressly prohibited.
dont.zh: 严禁将 AI 生成的文本作为个人原创作品提交；在哥大法学院规范下，严禁将非英语写作的机器翻译草稿作为原创英语成果提交。

dont.en: Do not enter Sensitive Data (PHI, PII, RHI) into tools lacking HIPAA BAAs like Workspace Gemini or unapproved commercial features, and do not use personal unvetted accounts for protected data.
dont.zh: 严禁将敏感数据（PHI、PII、RHI）输入缺乏 HIPAA BAA 的工具（如 Workspace 版 Gemini）或未经批准的商业功能，严禁使用个人未经审查的账户处理受保护数据。

scope.en: Covers Columbia University central Provost guidelines, CSSI Standards & Discipline 2026–2027 (adhering schools under Dean discretion), Columbia Law School 2026–2027 Default Academic Policy (with instructor written alternatives), Columbia Business School Honor Code, CUIMC Data Classification Matrix, and CUIT AI Services.
scope.zh: 涵盖哥伦比亚大学教务长总政策、CSSI 2026–2027《学生纪律规范》（依各院院长决定采纳之学院）、法学院 2026–2027 默认学术规范（教师可书面变更）、商学院荣誉准则、CUIMC 医疗数据分类矩阵及 CUIT 官方 AI 工具体系。

claim-columbia-001a.text: Columbia University has a university-wide Generative AI Policy from the Office of the Provost governing use by staff, faculty, students, and researchers, covering information security, data privacy, copyright, academic integrity, and bias.
claim-columbia-001a.scope: University-wide faculty, students, researchers, and staff under Provost guidance; operational discipline subject to school-level Dean adoption

evidence.quote: Since instructors and academic departments have the ability to develop their own AI course policies, students may encounter different guidelines across their courses. To avoid confusion, we encourage all instructors to include a clear, well-defined generative AI statement in their course syllabi that clearly delineates whether and how students can use AI in their coursework.

claim-columbia-004a.text: Under Columbia Law School's 2026–2027 Default Academic Policy on Student Use of AI (§9.1), use of AI during any examination is prohibited except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions; where not authorized, every word of an examination answer must be produced by the student without AI assistance (irrespective of whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten), and students are strictly forbidden from inputting current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns into an AI tool.
claim-columbia-004a.scope: Columbia Law School students in all JD, LLM, and JSD examinations

evidence.quote:
Examinations: Except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions, use of AI during any examination is prohibited.

- Every word of a student’s examination answer must be produced by that student without assistance from AI (including for English translation purposes). This prohibition encompasses all examinations, irrespective of format (i.e., whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten).

- Students are not permitted to input current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns from any course into an AI tool.

claim-columbia-004b.scope: Columbia Law School instructors; written alternative course/assignment policies for Sections8–11 defaults

evidence.quote: Default: The Rules set forth in Sections 8 through 11 of this Policy are considered defaults. claim-columbia-004c.text: Under Columbia Law School's 2026–2027 Policy (§8.3), students are permitted to consult AI to test arguments, solicit criticism, explore alternative articulations, and improve written work for clarity and reliability, alternate phrasing, and tone and concision, as well as identify and correct spelling and grammatical errors; in all cases students must exercise independent, rigorous critical judgment, and Sections 8–11 serve as default policies that instructors may vary in writing in the course syllabus or assignment instructions.
claim-columbia-004c.scope: Columbia Law School students in credit-bearing academic work

evidence.quote: Writing Support and Error Correction: Students are permitted to consult AI to test arguments, solicit criticism, and explore alternative articulations. Students may also use AI to improve their written work, including for clarity and reliability, alternate phrasing, and tone and concision. Students are also permitted to use AI tools to assist in identifying and correcting spelling and grammatical errors. In all of these cases, students are required to independently and rigorously assess the feedback generated by AI, using their own critical judgment to decide whether and how to implement any suggestions.

do.en: Check the UTOL assignment Permitted AI Use label (T0–T5 or Other) or course syllabus before using any generative AI tool.
do.zh: 使用任何生成式 AI 前，务必查阅 UTOL 作业页面上标注的「AI利用范围」标签（T0–T5 或 Other）或课程大纲说明。

do.en: Follow the instructor’s disclosure instructions; central guidance recommends asking students to name the AI tool used.
do.zh: 遵循教师的披露要求；中央指南建议教师要求学生注明使用的 AI 工具名称。

do.en: Use the institutional account specified for each service and check its data safeguards; no-training protection does not prove no retention.
do.zh: 使用各服务指定的机构账号并核对数据保护条件；不用于训练并不等于不留存。

dont.en: Never input personal information, confidential data, or unpublished research into AI tools; faculty must basically not input examination questions into language generation AI in unchanged form.
dont.zh: 切勿将个人信息、机密资料或未发表研究成果输入 AI 工具；教师原则上（基本的に）不得将考题以原样形式输入语言生成式 AI。

dont.en: Do not copy and paste AI-generated answers and submit them as your own work; unauthorized submission violates academic integrity.
dont.zh: 严禁将 AI 生成的解答全盘复制粘贴并作为原创作业提交；未授权提交构成学术不端。

dont.en: Do not assume institutional tool access (Copilot, Gemini, Zoom, Slack) grants permission to use AI in coursework or examinations.
dont.zh: 切勿将拥有校级 AI 工具访问权限（Copilot、Gemini、Zoom、Slack）误认为具备课程考核使用许可。

scope.en: UTOL LMS mandatory assignment Permitted AI Use setting (effective Sept. 29, 2026), Taura EVP 6-level taxonomy (T0–T5 / Other), instructor coursework discretion, disclosure recommendations, campus-wide Copilot and Gemini commercial data protection, and research misconduct procedure under Rule No. 79 (qualified in principle).

draft-u-tokyo-008.text: Under official faculty guidance and student notices, students and faculty are cautioned against information leakage: students must never input confidential information, personal information, or unpublished research results into AI tools due to potential leakage or model training use, and faculty are instructed that examination questions, being highly confidential documents, must basically (基本的に) not be input into language-generating AI in unchanged form. The separate 'Security Guidelines for Generative AI Use' (March 12, 2024) require internal UTokyo Account authentication and are held as an unverified private source.
draft-u-tokyo-008.scope: Student coursework, confidential/personal data, unpublished research results, and faculty examination preparation (examination questions basically not in unchanged form; March 12 security guidelines held as internal-auth source)

draft-u-tokyo-009.text: Under Rule No. 79 (東京大学科学研究行動規範委員会規則), formal scientific research misconduct investigations establish procedural timelines qualified in principle (原則として): the preliminary inquiry results must be reported to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving an allegation (Art. 8(5)); the Investigation Committee commences formal investigation in principle within 30 days of the decision to investigate (Art. 9(2)); the Committee makes its adjudication determination in principle within 150 days of starting formal investigation (Art. 11(1)); respondent defense opportunity is granted in principle within 14 days of receiving draft determination notification (Art. 11(7)); and a respondent against whom misconduct was determined may file an objection/appeal to the Committee Chair in principle within 30 days of receiving the determination notice under Art. 11(11) (Art. 12(1)). These clocks apply exclusively to scientific research misconduct proceedings and do not govern undergraduate or generic coursework discipline.
draft-u-tokyo-009.scope: Scientific research activities and formal research misconduct investigations under Rule No. 79 (distinct from undergraduate/coursework discipline; all clocks qualified in principle)

evidence.quote: この規則は、科学研究に携わる東京大学(以下「本学」という。)の教職員及び本学の施設設備を利用して研究活動を行う者(以下「研究者」という。)を対象として、本学の科学研究における行動規範(以下「行動規範」という。)に違反する不正行為(過去に研究者であった者が、研究者であった時期に行った不正行為を含む。以下同じ。)に対処し、行動規範の遵守を促すための委員会の設置及び不正行為に対する措置等について定める。
